title: Let Him Go to Win Him Over

source.chapter: Let Him Go to Win Him Over
source.quote: Press him and he turns on you; let him run and his force drains. Follow close but do not crowd him, wear down his strength and break his will, and take him when he is spent.

moral: Push too hard and he fights back; ease off and it works.

story.title: Too Close
story.text: Chased too hard, the man ahead turned around to fight.
story.narration: In the year 225, on a mountain road in the south, Meng Huo ran and Zhuge Liang followed. Press too hard and the man ahead turns and fights with all he has — the old military books call it "press him and he turns on you".

story.title: Ease Off
story.text: He eased off, and the man ahead slowed down on his own.
story.narration: Zhuge Liang had his men drop back a little and follow at an easy distance. Mile after mile, the man ahead used up his strength and slowed down by himself — he was not caught; he gave in.

keyMoment.question: He keeps running. How do you make him stop?

options.hint: Press him and he turns and fights; nobody gives in.

options.text: Follow him, but never too close — wait until he is worn out

options.hint: Stop chasing and he is gone for good.

keyMoment.reveal: Press too hard and he fights back; ease off and it works — follow him until he gives in, and he stops by himself.

misconceptions: The closer you chase, the sooner you catch him
To make someone yield, you have to grab him

quiz.question: While you are chasing, how far behind should you stay?
options: Not too close, not too far — keep him in that band
As close as you can, right behind him
As far as you can, out of his sight
quiz.explanation: Too close and he fights back and gets his strength again; too far and you lose him and waste the chase. Stay in the band and his strength keeps draining.

quiz.question: The kitten is hiding under the sofa and will not come out. What do you do?
options: Sit a little way off and wait for it to come out
Reach in and pull it out
quiz.explanation: Reach in and it only hides deeper. Sit a little way off and wait, and it will poke its head out by itself.
